hints: Because the lorry moves up the hill at constant speed, the acceleration is zero, so the driving force balances the resistance plus the component of weight down the slope.
Calculate the down-slope component of weight: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\theta = 12\,000(10)(0.08)$.
Sum the resistance of $1500\text{ N}$ and the weight component to obtain the forward driving force $F_{\text{D}}$.
Use the power formula $P = F_{\text{D}} \times v$ with $v = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to show that $P = 55.5\text{ kW}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the component of the lorry's weight acting down the incline with $m = 12\,000\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\sin\theta = 0.08$:
$$W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\theta = 12\,000(10)(0.08) = 9600\text{ N}$$

Find the forward driving force $F_{\text{D}}$ balancing resistance and weight at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$F_{\text{D}} = R + mg\sin\theta = 1500 + 9600 = 11\,100\text{ N}$$

Calculate the power of the engine using $P = F_{\text{D}} \times v$ with $v = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 11\,100 \times 5 = 55\,500\text{ W} = 55.5\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State Newton's second law along the incline for the lorry moving at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma = 0$$
The forces acting parallel to the slope are the forward driving force $F_{\text{D}}$, the opposing resistance $R = 1500\text{ N}$, and the down-slope component of weight $mg\sin\theta$:
$$F_{\text{D}} - R - mg\sin\theta = 0$$
$$F_{\text{D}} = R + mg\sin\theta$$

State the relationship between power, driving force, and velocity:
$$P = F_{\text{D}} v$$
Substitute $F_{\text{D}} = 11\,100\text{ N}$ and constant speed $v = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 11\,100 \times 5 = 55\,500\text{ W}$$
Convert watts to kilowatts by dividing by $1000$:
$$P = \frac{55\,500}{1000} = 55.5\text{ kW}$$
Thus the power of the engine is $55.5\text{ kW}$.

hints: The resistance model is given as $R = kv^2$.
Use the known condition from part (i) that when $v = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the resistance is $1500\text{ N}$.
Substitute these values into $R = kv^2$ and solve for $k$.
walkthrough:
Substitute $v = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and resistance $R = 1500\text{ N}$ into the resistance formula $R = kv^2$:
$$1500 = k(5^2)$$
$$25k = 1500$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the given resistance law relating magnitude of resistance to speed:
$$R = kv^2$$
From part (i), at a speed of $v = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the resistance force is $1500\text{ N}$.

Substitute $R = 1500\text{ N}$ and $v = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ into the equation:
$$1500 = k(5)^2$$
$$1500 = 25k$$

hints: On a level road, there is no weight component along the direction of motion, so at constant speed the driving force equals resistance: $F_{\text{D}} = 60v^2$.
Express power in terms of velocity: $P = F_{\text{D}} \times v = (60v^2)v = 60v^3$.
Set $60v^3$ equal to $55\,500\text{ W}$ and solve for $v$.
walkthrough:
On a level road at constant speed, the driving force equals the resistance force:
$$F_{\text{D}} = R = 60v^2$$

Substitute into the power equation $P = F_{\text{D}} \times v$ with $P = 55.5\text{ kW} = 55\,500\text{ W}$:
$$55\,500 = (60v^2)v = 60v^3$$
teacher_walkthrough: On a straight level road, gravity acts purely perpendicularly to the road, so there is no gravitational component along the direction of motion.

Because the lorry moves at constant speed ($a = 0$), Newton's second law states that the net horizontal force is zero:
$$F_{\text{D}} - R = 0 \implies F_{\text{D}} = R$$
Using the resistance model $R = 60v^2$, the driving force is:
$$F_{\text{D}} = 60v^2$$

State the power equation relating power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = F_{\text{D}} v$$
Substitute $F_{\text{D}} = 60v^2$:
$$P = (60v^2) \times v = 60v^3$$

Given that the engine maintains a power of $55.5\text{ kW} = 55\,500\text{ W}$, set up the cubic equation:
$$60v^3 = 55\,500$$
Divide both sides by $60$:
$$v^3 = \frac{55\,500}{60} = 925$$
Take the cube root of both sides:
$$v = (925)^{1/3} \approx 9.7435\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 9.74\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus the speed of the lorry on the level road is $9.74\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
